subject.title: Gateway restart drops queued and in-flight inbound messages

question: Which restart message-recovery path should own this issue: the SQLite followup queue PR, the SIGUSR1 drain mitigation, or a successor design that also covers drain-window and channel ACK behavior?
rationale: Durable replay changes persistent runtime state and cross-channel delivery semantics, and there are multiple open candidate PRs with different scopes and risk profiles.

options.title: Advance SQLite followup persistence
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82572 or a refreshed successor as the primary fix for durable queued-followup recovery, then track drain-window and channel ACK work separately.

options.title: Land only SIGUSR1 drain mitigation
options.body: Prioritize https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/46303 as a smaller mitigation while leaving full durable replay unresolved.

options.title: Pause for broader restart design
options.body: Wait for a unified restart recovery/API decision before merging any phase-one persistence branch.

recommendation.title: Advance SQLite followup persistence
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82572 or a refreshed successor as the primary fix for durable queued-followup recovery, then track drain-window and channel ACK work separately.

likelyOwner.reason: The restart-drain and gateway lifecycle history makes this the best available owner for choosing the durable recovery direction.
